findings: None of the full-evidence responses gives a complete source-grounded status answer. Many are offers or greetings; others answer a different question or claim unverified live access.
A source report of past file placement does not establish that all files are currently visible or that the assistant checked or repaired access.
The same relevant utterances remain at fixed recording times across the full-evidence context positions, so adding earlier history does not vary the retention interval after those facts.

All 120 primary adequacy ratings are 1 or 2; no source-reviewed full-evidence response supplies a complete grounded status answer. This agreement on the coarse failure conclusion does not validate every ordinal rating.
limitations: No independent human annotation or acoustic listening rating.
No override of local-LLM scores; numerical disagreements must remain visible.
Selected substantive disagreement examples are not an exhaustive human-labelled accuracy set.
